item.title: Cross-Domain Solutions: Explaining What Nobody Would
item.description: Cross-domain solutions are one of those topics where the gap between “people who know” and “people who need to know” is enormous. If you’re an architect or engineer who’s been told you need a CDS in your design, good luck finding a clear explanation of what that actually means.

item.title: Data-Centric Security: Building a Knowledge Resource
item.description: I’ve been working in and around data-centric security for a while now. It’s a topic that matters enormously — especially in coalition and multi-national contexts where you need data to flow between organisations at different classification levels, while the security travels with the data rather than relying on perimeter controls.

item.title: Giving MSP's access to your keys? They should be automating..
item.description: Recently reading a blog post on the NCSC blog regarding how organisations should choose their managed service proviers (MSP’s) I found the guidance (while appropriate) not as in-depth as I would want to be in recipt of if I was a public sector customer looking to choose an MSP that was ‘right for me’.

item.title: Bringing security controls into CI/CD with IaC scanning
item.description: In a recent blog post I wrote about the overall controls that can be built into your CI/CD pipelines to increase your security posture.

item.title: Securing your CI/CD Pipelines
item.description: When speaking to customers about security, I always try to raise the topic of shifting security left. This relatively moden practice and thinking comes from the dual need to not only (a) de-burden the security team from the low-value tasks of approving individual changes, and (b) allowing the software engineering teams inside the organisation to increase the speed of change, while keeping the security bar high.

item.title: Sa Associate Notes
item.description: Update as of March 2022 - I have now achieved AWS SA Associate, AWS SA Professional and AWS Security Speciality certifications. My experience has so far been that all three associate qualifications combined effectively produce one SA Pro, and the move from SA pro into the specialty certifications is not large, and geenrally involves going only a little deeper.

item.title: Job Move
item.description: Having spent 4 months deciding that I wanted to leave, and a further 4 months applying for a job with AWS, Friday the 5th of June marks my last day as a principal consultant at InfinityWorks, the end of a four year journey in which I have learned more than I thought possible.
